text:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT - model_load_failure on prod-us-west-2 gw-3. Multiple model warmup failures -> route /v1/generate experiencing errors. Affected pods: runtime-xyz-*. Error sample linked: https://logs.prod/redwood/2234567890

eric: oncall here, paging in. I'll grab logs and coordinate.

maya: seeing repeated CUDA allocation failures in warmup: 
```
E 03:12:04 runtime: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory while allocating 11.8 GiB
E 03:12:10 model_deserialize: EOF while reading weights (offset 0x1f4a000)
E 03:14:05 compile_step: timeout after 120s waiting for kernel compile
```

jin: kube events show OOMKilled on compute-12, then container restarts. Node also reported GPU reset 3x (nvidia-driver). Node flapped, pods rescheduled.

samir: stack: model loader fails during deserialization when compile cache can't be read. Disk pressure on /var/cache/compile seems likely. Logs: 
```
WARNING: compile-cache eviction triggered (free space < 1GB)
ERROR: open /var/cache/compile/model-x/cache.bin: no space left on device
```

luis: flagging customer impact: two enterprise tenants (acct-332, acct-411) saw 503s and ~2-3s extra tail latency on fallback requests. CS notified.

eric: immediate mitigations I'm applying: 1) map heavy routes to small-quant fallback, 2) cordon+drain compute-12, 3) reduce max_concurrency on runtime pods from 16->6, 4) disable large batch window. Executing now.

maya: commands I'm running: 
```bash
kubectl cordon node/compute-12
kubectl drain node/compute-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# restart runtime on other nodes to flush bad kernels
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime -n prod --selector=zone=us-west-2
```

deploy-bot: automated-fallback applied: route /v1/generate -> gpt-7b-quant-legacy for enterprise tiers. Change id: fb-2234.

jin: note - restarting runtime pods triggered a few additional model load compiles; compile cache still thrashing. I cleared old compile cache on two nodes: 
```bash
ssh node-21 sudo rm -rf /var/tmp/compile-cache/*
ssh node-22 sudo rm -rf /var/tmp/compile-cache/*
```
That freed ~15GB. GPU resets decreased.

samir: proposal: do NOT increase model_load_timeout globally. Instead: keep shorter timeouts, prefer model substitution + reduce concurrency. Increasing timeouts only delays failures and blocks worker slots.

eric: agreed. Rolling back the recent model bundle that added large custom kernels (commit 1a2b3c). Reverting to last-known-good.

maya: revert command executed: revert-model-commit 1a2b3c -> 0f9e7d. Deploying rollback to canary first.

incident-bot: Status update: severity -> P2. Success ratio for /v1/generate improved from 86% -> 99.2% in last 10m.

luis: customer impact summary for incident report: two customers impacted, ETA of full recovery ~15-30m after fallback. Error window ~40m from first alert. Started outreach at 03:25 UTC.

eric: preparing handoff to night oncall jin. Handoff notes: compute-12 drained and cordoned, fallback mapping active (fb-2234), compile-cache cleared on two replacement nodes, monitor for further GPU resets, watch compile-timeout counts and disk pressure on /var/cache. Action items: 1) investigate why compile cache grew without evict policy, 2) add alert for compile-cache free space < 5GB, 3) run model bundle regression tests before next canary.

jin: ack taking over. I will keep watch on node GPU resets and success rates, and follow up on postmortem doc. Will coordinate with infra for driver upgrades if we see more resets. :thumbsup: 

eric: filing incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime + eng-sre for postmortem. Tagging owners: @maya @samir.

samir: quick note — logs also show a few deserialization EOFs that correlate with abrupt pod restarts; need to ensure model artifact uploads are atomic (tmp -> final rename) to avoid partial reads during rolling updates. Adding to RCA.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged by eric. Next update expected 30m or on-change.

luis: thanks all — I'll draft the customer-facing summary and attach to the incident ticket.

jin: will run a quick healthcheck: eval traffic through fallback -> 10k requests/min test, check p95 latency, and compile-timeout count. Posting results in 10m.

eric: good handoff. logging out.

(End of thread)
